thread:
tina: FYI prepping presales deck for Soteria Health POC (call 11am). Key asks: EU-only compute, HSM BYOK, subprocessors by region, and a short note on failover behavior.

omar-se: Which EU regions do they want? They mentioned eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 but asked if eu-west can be preferred.

tina: They prefer eu-west-1, but want a documented fallback model if we hit capacity.

ben-ops: Current hosted tenant pinning supports eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. We can mark eu-west as primary but if capacity is exhausted we will either queue or failover to eu-central depending on customer's failover flag. No automatic non-EU failover for EU-pinned tenants.

omar-se: Can we state that in RFP language? Need something short.

ben-ops: Suggested text: "Tenant compute and inference will be executed in customer-designated EU regions. If the designated region is temporarily capacity-constrained, requests will be queued and may failover to another EU-designated region only if the customer has enabled cross-region failover. Redwood will not route EU-pinned traffic to non-EU regions without explicit customer authorization."

lia-legal: Good. On BYOK/HSM: HSM-backed customer keys are supported for Private and Dedicated deployments only. For hosted we offer partner KMS key-wrapping (software KMS) with attestation for approved customers; HSM BYOK in the shared hosted offering is not supported. We'll include a migration path note.

tina: They insist on HSM now. How do we explain migration and downtime?

ben-ops: Migration path: move from Hosted (wrapped KMS) -> Dedicated (HSM) via data-plane rebind. For stateless inference, expect minimal interruption (a few seconds) to rebind endpoints; for workloads with KV cache expect a short warm-up window (minutes) post-cutover. We'll provide runbook steps.

omar-se: Subprocessors list we can share? Need exact names for the questionnaire.

ben-ops: EU subprocessors: AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), ObservabilityCo (metrics/logs EU), KeyWrap Partners Ltd (KMS wrapping in eu-central). APAC: EdgeCloud (ap-southeast-1 beta).

lia-legal: Draft questionnaire bullet: "Redwood engages subprocessors necessary to operate regional compute (cloud provider), telemetry (observability), and key management partners. A region-mapped Subprocessor Addendum will be attached. Redwood provides 30 days' notice for subprocessor additions and an opt-out for material changes."

tina: They also asked for IP ranges for allowlisting and a CI that proves egress stays in EU.

ben-ops: Provide this minimal CIDR block list for presales: EU frontends 34.224.0.0/14; EU egress gateways 44.200.128.0/17; KMS partner endpoints 3.122.77.0/24. For technical assurance we can provide network diagrams and signed attestation from our KMS partner (pending their approval).

tina: Pricing: can we give a ballpark delta for Dedicated+HSM vs Hosted EU-pin?

omar-se: Ballpark: Hosted EU-pin = list * 1.2 (isolation uplift). Dedicated reserved = ~3x per throughput unit. One-off HSM onboarding ~ $12k-18k depending on provider. Note: exact pricing requires workload profile.

infra-bot: NOTE: KMS attestation workflow created - ticket INF-9981.

tina: Great. Last ask: they want a 1-pager for their security team summarizing subprocessors, BYOK options, CIDRs, data deletion/audit retention, and failover behavior. Lia, can you draft?

lia-legal: Yes, I'll draft the 1-pager and attach the Subprocessor Addendum. ETA EOD today.

tina: Thanks all, I'll synthesize into a 2-page presales PDF and upload to the deal room before the call. :thumbsup:
